text.p: A planned alliance between Philipp Holzmann and Hochtief AG, Germany's two largest construction groups, could cost up to 6,000 jobs, building union IG Bau said on Monday.

In a letter to work councils at the two companies, IG Bau chief Klaus Wiesehuegel also attacked German banking giant Deutsche Bank for facilitating the deal by "pooling" its 25.1 percent voting interest in Holzmann with a 24.9 percent stake held by Hochtief.
"Jobs are being sacrificed to the short-term quest for yields," he said in the letter.

Holzmann and Hochtief together employ some 52,000 staff. An IG Bau spokesman said the job loss forecast referred only to their domestic workforces, which currently total 23,000. Any cooperation would clearly hit central administration posts and labour-intensive activities hardest, he added.

A Holzmann spokesman said the figure of 6,000 job losses "was devoid of any foundation" and that while some personnel costs could be saved as part of the cooperation, the aim was to increase overall business and employment.

The two groups said at a news conference in March that the deal was initially intended to allow them to cooperate in international markets before exploring whether synergies in their domestic market were available and permissable.

Hochtief said at the time such cooperation was an inevitable part of a rather late restructuring of the German construction sector, currently suffering from price pressure and stagnant demand which has resulted in deep unemployment.

The deal requires the approval of European cartel authorities and the German Federal Cartel Office, which has long opposed attempts by Hochtief to increase its influence in Holzmann, has said it is asking for adjudication of the case to be returned to it.
